passages.note: First-person account of his HB 1002 amendment to bar further IEDC sales tax exemptions for data centers; per the annex, opposing a data-centre tax break shows only the side against rung 5, not a rung, and no record page of the amendment is supplied.

Caucus release quoting his complaint about data-centre sales tax exemptions; the third-person report of his vote and amendment is context, not a record, and HB 1002 (88-4) would be near-unanimous anyway.

Opposition to HB 1333's automatic farmland approvals without hearings is framed as local control and public input, which the annex treats as adjacent; it names no moratorium, cost bar, approval conditions or disclosure.
Forum answers on energy, the IEDC and the LEAP district never address data centers or the rungs' conditions.

rows.reasoning: His own words oppose sales tax exemptions for data centers ("prevented the Indiana Economic Development Corporation (IEDC) from granting any further sales tax exemptions to data centers"), which shows a side against "welcoming data center investment with minimal regulatory barriers" but does not choose among a moratorium, a bar on passing costs to residential customers, or pre-approval impact assessments, cost-sharing and community benefits. His HB 1333 objections concern local control and hearings, which are adjacent.

quotes.text: It also would have prevented the Indiana Economic Development Corporation (IEDC) from granting any further sales tax exemptions to data centers.
Apparently, it’s fine for trillion-dollar corporations to pay no sales tax on energy use at their data centers.
This vote further weakens local control and shuts Hoosiers out of decisions that affect their own communities.
